objectives: Recognise taught CVC word families containing l.
Decode words by noticing shared rimes.
Read controlled l word-family chains accurately.
Build automatic recognition without guessing from pictures.
concepts: A word family shares a common rime.
Changing the onset can create a new CVC word.
Controlled reading keeps decoding within taught sound patterns.

definitions.definition: The initial consonant sound or consonant cluster before the vowel in a syllable.
The vowel and following sounds in a syllable.
A group of words sharing the same rime.

workedExamples: lip, sip, tip share the -ip rime.
lap, map, tap share the -ap rime.
log, dog, fog share the -og rime.
commonMistakes: Guessing from the first letter or a picture.
Changing more than the onset when reading a word family.

basic: Read taught l CVC word-family chains.
conceptual: Identify shared rimes and changing onsets.
application: Decode a new taught-pattern word using its family.
higherOrderThinking: Explain why changing one onset preserves the rime.
mixedReview: Mix l word families with previously taught CVC families.

quickRevision: find rime → say onset → blend → reread
mistakeBasedRevision: If a word is misread, isolate the rime and rebuild the onset + rime blend.
weakTopicRevision: Practise the weakest word family with fresh controlled words.

activities.name: Word-family sort
steps: Place it with matching family members.

activities.name: Onset swap
steps: Check that the rime stayed the same.

outcomes: Learner decodes controlled CVC words using shared rimes.
Learner reads taught-pattern word lists accurately and begins building automaticity.

questions.question: A learner reads “lip” correctly but struggles with “sip.” What should be practised?
options: Keep the -ip pattern and change only the first sound.
